about: The input device used at start: the saved device when it is connected, otherwise the system default, otherwise the first device; nothing when there are none (Swift inputDeviceToUse(in:savedUID:systemDefaultUID:), Python input_device_to_use). Each case: the connected 'devices' in order, the 'saved' device and the system 'default' (null: none), and the device 'expect'ed (null: none). Devices are named by the keys of 'devices'; each edition maps a key to a device of its own. 'editions' limits a row to the editions that can express it: the web asks the browser for the saved device, then for the default, and the browser always resolves a default itself — so it has no first-device step, and with no inputs nothing can be opened. The web runs its rows through its engine with a fake browser. Expected values are Swift's. The rest of test/mic-selection (MS6 on) drives the engine and stays as code.

inputDeviceToUse.note: the saved device wins when it is present — over the system default, and over any other device
the saved device is not connected — the system default
nothing saved — the system default, not a device listed ahead of it (BlackHole)
no usable system default — the first device; the browser always resolves a default
no devices — nothing; in the browser, with no inputs nothing can be opened
